chunks: What Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Saʿīd ibn Janāḥ, from some of our companions, from al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed, Abū al-Khaṭṭāb had corrupted most of the people of al-Kūfah, and they would not perform the maghrib salat (prayer) until the twilight had disappeared. That applies only to the traveler, the fearful one, and the one with a need.

key_terms.أَبَا الْخَطَّابِ: Abū al-Khaṭṭāb, identified here as the one who misled many people of al-Kūfah
key_terms.الشَّفَقُ: the twilight glow whose disappearance marks a later time
key_terms.الْخَائِفِ: the fearful person, for whom this delay is permitted
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبَ: the maghrib salat (prayer), the sunset prayer
key_terms.الْمُسَافِرِ: the traveler, for whom this delay is permitted
key_terms.صَاحِبِ الْحَاجَةِ: a person with a pressing need or necessity

ai.seo_question: When is it permissible to delay the maghrib salat (prayer) until after the twilight disappears?
ai.summary: This hadith states that delaying the maghrib salat (prayer) until the disappearance of twilight was a corrupt practice spread among many people of al-Kūfah by Abū al-Khaṭṭāb. It clarifies that such delay is only allowed for specific categories: the traveler, the fearful person, and one occupied by a pressing need.
